contradictions_noticed: Approval routing: the BRD requires routing EVERY request to the employee's direct manager, but the kickoff proposes auto-approving single-day casual leave with no manager step. It was explicitly flagged as undecided, and HR still wants an audit trail even if approval is automatic.

Casual-leave carry-over: Meera (email 4) says unused casual leave must lapse at year-end with no carry-over, while Anil (email 6) says the handbook allows carrying over up to 5 unused casual days. Unresolved; a HR/Ops/Finance meeting was requested.

Approval model: the BRD describes a single direct-manager approval, whereas the kickoff calls for a flexible, department-specific flow with different chains and possibly multiple approval levels (plus escalation to the manager's manager).
Mobile scope status: the BRD treats mobile-browser support as a firm in-scope requirement (scope statement plus a 375px Chrome/Safari NFR), but the kickoff treats mobile as an unscoped 'want / TBD'.

Holiday calendar: the BRD and the legacy notes assume the existing holiday calendar will be reused (settled), but the kickoff and Jira ELAMS-40 treat 'reuse vs build new' as an open, unresolved question.

Manager approval channel: the BRD describes a dedicated in-app pending-approvals queue for managers, while the kickoff insists managers will not log into a separate portal and must approve/reject from the email itself.

Deployment/access model: the legacy notes describe an on-prem, corporate-network-only system with no public-internet exposure and no mobile access, which conflicts with the to-be requirements for mobile-browser access for a largely deskless workforce and India (Asia-South) cloud-region data storage.
